name: The Noor Project
mission: The Noor Project works towards overcoming poverty, illness, and illiteracy with both short and long-term approaches. Our mission is rooted in self-sufficiency, empowering poverty-stricken communities with tools and resources including education, mindset training, and employment.
theoryOfChange: We aim at the root causes of poverty among families in Pakistan to stop the cycle from repeating. We enroll families into programs that meet their needs. Once their member graduates from our vocational course and secures employment, the family is taken off the list for the ration packets and the empty spot is given to another family in need.

rich_narrative.summary: For the Needy & Hungry Foundation Inc, operating as The Noor Project, focuses on lifting marginalized families out of poverty in Pakistan through a multi-sector approach. The organization reported <cite id="2">total revenue of $1,759,964 in fiscal year 2023</cite>, reflecting a significant <cite id="2">three-year revenue growth rate of 29.6%</cite>. Its operations are centered on providing direct services, including a <cite id="1">grammar school, health clinic, pharmacy, and technical training</cite> to foster self-sufficiency. While the organization demonstrates high financial efficiency with a <cite id="1">100.0% program expense ratio</cite>, it faces governance challenges. Specifically, the <cite id="2">board of directors consists of only one member</cite>, which limits independent oversight. Furthermore, <cite id="2">no financial filings newer than FY2023 are available</cite>, meaning donors should treat this three-year-old financial picture with caution. Despite these gaps, the charity maintains a <cite id="1">Silver Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite> and provides a <cite id="3">zakat calculator to assist Muslim donors</cite> in fulfilling their religious obligations. The charity's model is highly direct, claiming to have reached <cite id="1">440,000 beneficiaries</cite> with an efficient <cite id="1">cost of approximately $3.48 per beneficiary</cite>.
